selectedTopic: Rubber hex dumbbell mold parting lines, flash, surface pits and trim-damage inspection
selectionReason: Public results and community questions repeatedly confuse normal molding witnesses with cracks, while industry guidance separates parting-line location, flash thickness and extension, pits, blisters, cuts and tears. The site lacked a buyer-side guide linking these names to zones, samples, evidence and lot disposition.

competitors.name: Protolabs
competitors.observation: Explains parting lines, flash and knit-line consequences in molded parts. The guide adds dumbbell zones, sample approval and lot decisions without transferring plastic-part tolerances.

competitors.name: Vicone / ARPM RMA guidance
competitors.observation: Defines flash thickness and extension and stresses design-manufacturer agreement. ChinaFreeWeight applies that decision pattern without inventing numeric dumbbell limits.

competitors.name: Bick inspection guide
competitors.observation: Search-visible dumbbell inspection content discusses cosmetic lines and flash, confirming buyer intent. Its tolerances and commercial claims were not reused.

competitors.name: Rubber molding troubleshooting pages
competitors.observation: Industry pages connect flash and surface imperfections to tooling and process factors. The article stays at buyer-observable evidence and does not diagnose a factory from one photo.

rejectedTopics: Rubber coating peeling and cracking — a dedicated guide already owns coating adhesion and separation.
Rubber odor and emissions — an existing multilingual guide owns sensory comparison and evidence boundaries.
Rubber Shore hardness — a dedicated guide owns durometer method and interpretation.
Surface bloom and oily residue — an existing guide owns residue classification and receiving decisions.
Dumbbell head alignment and joint retention — dedicated guides own geometry and hidden head-to-handle construction.
siteGaps: No dedicated guide distinguished a normal mold parting line from excess flash, pits, blisters, trim cuts, tears and open separation while connecting each finding to head zones, photographs, severity and lot disposition.

sources.title: ISO 3302-1:2014 — Rubber tolerances for products
sources.use: Official current standard record used to establish dimensional-tolerance and flash-classification scope without selecting a universal dumbbell grade.

sources.title: ARPM/RMA molded-rubber quality guidance
sources.use: Industry guidance used to distinguish flash thickness, flash extension and parting-line designation; no generic numeric class is imposed on dumbbells.

sources.title: Protolabs — Injection molding defects
sources.use: Manufacturing explanation used to separate an expected parting line from knit lines and other process conditions in stressed zones.

sources.title: GE Vernova cosmetic inspection guidance
sources.use: Industry defect vocabulary reviewed for flash, fracture and surface marks; no acceptance number was transferred to free weights.

sources.use: Used only to confirm recurring buyer wording about seams, cracks near handles and whether visible damage is serviceable.

limitations: Quora pages were blocked from automated verification and supplied no claims.
